reviews.reasoning: Span tiles exactly onto WEB 103:1-5 with no gap or overlap at the 5|6 seam (confirmed against the cluster's own tiling: verses 1-22 tile 103 exactly across the five rows). Psalm 103 is an identity psalm: the superscription inventory records its title as mt_title_verses "prefix_of_v1" (label le_david), so "By David." sitting inside MT v.1 rather than as a separate counted title verse is correct, and the dual-cite web:Ps.103.0 = oshb:Ps.103.1 is the right form for a +0-shift title (no range needed, unlike the four +2 psalms). Both curly-quoted WEB verses and the Hebrew clause were independently re-spliced from source and re-collated at byte tier against oshb:Ps.103.1 (byte match confirmed). The 5|6 boundary holds independently: verses 1-5 stay inside the participial/imperative complex governed by the v.1-2 summons (second-person address to the soul, with the forgiving/healing/redeeming/crowning/satisfying participles all modifying the addressee), while v.6 opens a fresh independent declarative naming Yahweh as grammatical subject. rejected_alternative correctly identifies and rebuts the only serious rival (reading v.1 as title overflow). No factual, tier, or evidentiary defect found.

Span tiles exactly onto WEB 103:6-10 with no gap or overlap at either seam. The morphological claim ("executes" as a participial predicate at oshb:Ps.103.6, contrasted with the imperative clause opening oshb:Ps.103.1) was independently re-derived from the pointed bytes, since the staged extract carries no morphology layer: the qal participle pattern is legible directly in the consonantal-plus-vocalic shape of the cited word, and the contrast with the second-person imperative of v.1 holds. Quotes verified byte-true and verbatim-checked against the WEB verse text. The 10|11 boundary this row shares with the next span is well-marked independently: v.11 opens a comparative-simile construction (heaven-height / east-west / father-compassion) that v.6-10's declarative catalog does not use, so the seam is not merely asserted but structurally real. confidence medium is appropriately calibrated: the discourse-register shift is a real but not formally unambiguous marker, and no stronger rival seam sits one verse away in either direction. No defect found.

Span tiles exactly onto WEB 103:11-14. Quotes verified byte-true. This row's own device_notes and rejected_alternative honestly surface the genuinely contestable seam at 14|15 (the dust motif forward-links to the grass/flower motif that opens the next span), and independent re-derivation from the pointed bytes confirms the writer's rebuttal is sound rather than asserted: v.14's verbs ("he knows"/"he remembers") keep the same third-person referent (Yahweh, continuing from v.13's explicit divine name) that governs the whole compassion-simile chain from v.11, while v.15 introduces a distinct fresh grammatical subject ("man") not present anywhere in 11-14. That is a legitimate discourse/subject-frame argument, not mere taste, and the thematic dust-to-grass linkage the rejected_alternative concedes is real texture rather than a superior tier-1 warrant one verse away. No basis to overturn the seam. confidence medium matches the row's own disclosed uncertainty. No defect found.

challenges.claim: The rationale overstates the scope of the divergence between the v.1 and v.22 barchi-nafshi clauses: it states they "differ only in the trailing accent mark on the final word," but independently re-spliced and re-collated, the two clauses carry different cantillation on the first word and the second word as well, not solely the final word; the skeleton-identical claim the row actually rests its argument on is correct, but the supporting description of where the difference sits is not.
challenges.evidence: Programmatically spliced (word-indexed, not hand-typed) from verse_map_oshb.json and independently re-collated against source at byte tier (collate.py, GREEN): the mid-verse clause at oshb:Ps.103.1 is בָּרֲכִ֣י נַ֭פְשִׁי אֶת יְהוָ֑ה and the verse-final clause at oshb:Ps.103.22 is בָּרֲכִ֥י נַ֝פְשִׁ֗י אֶת יְהוָֽה (both byte-verified substrings of their cited verses). At NFD tier these differ at three word positions, not one: word 1's trope mark (U+05A3 munah in v.1 vs U+05A5 merkha in v.22), word 2's trope marks (one mark in v.1 vs two, U+059D+U+0597, in v.22), and word 4's trailing mark (U+0591 etnachta, stripped as ordinary cantillation, in v.1 vs U+05BD, retained as meteg/silluq, in v.22). Stripping cantillation (accent_stripped tier) removes the word-1 and word-2 differences and leaves exactly one difference, the retained final-word mark -- so "only the final word" is true of the accent_stripped comparison the row does not name, not of the raw pointed text as stated. Stripping vowels too (skeleton tier) the two clauses are identical, which is the tier the row correctly claims and the tier its boundary argument actually needs.
